# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Pick | Why | Price in the sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** (best overall) | Runner's World's top pick. WIRED says it has the clearest sound of the clip-ons and physical buttons that are easier to use mid-run. 7 hr battery (about 19.5 hr with case), IPX4. | $199 (down from $299) |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** (best bone conduction) | Leaves your ears fully open. 12 hr battery, IP55, physical buttons. Fuller bass than older bone-conduction models. | $125-$180, depending on retailer |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** (best for long runs) | 10 hr battery (40 hr with case), IP57. WIRED's overall pick. | $200 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** (best value for running) | SoundGuys' top open-ear pick, with strong bass for the category and an IP54 rating. | $99 (down from $149) |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** (best budget hook-style) | IP55, ear hook, 10 hr battery (42 hr with case). | $79.99 at Amazon per SoundGuys |
| **JLab Flex Open** (cheapest way to try the style) | Less bass and detail, but comfortable and stable. | About $40 |

**Where to buy**

- Bose Ultra Open: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) has Bose, Amazon, and Walmart links. [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) lists Bose and Best Buy.
- Shokz OpenRun Pro 2: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/) links Amazon, REI, and Best Buy. [RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946) links Best Buy and Walmart.
- Shokz OpenDots 2: [WIRED's guide](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) links Amazon, Best Buy, and Shokz.
- Nothing Ear (Open) and Soundcore AeroFit 2: [SoundGuys' open-ear roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) links Amazon for both.
- JLab Flex Open: [Runner's World guide](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) links Amazon and Walmart.

**How to choose**

- **Maximum awareness:** Bone conduction (OpenRun Pro 2) keeps your ears the most open. Runner's World warns the neckband can clash with long hair, ponytails, and winter hats.
- **Best sound:** The Bose Ultra Open. Runner's World noted it can be a bit quiet in heavy traffic, and it has the shortest battery life and lowest water resistance of the group.
- **Rain and long runs:** The OpenDots 2 has the best battery and water resistance listed here.
- **Tight budget:** The AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open. Runner's World says the Flex Open is the lowest-risk way to see if you like clip-ons.

**Notes**

- Runner's World says Bose plans to release a new pair of open-ear earbuds within about a month of its Sept. 23 update. If you're set on Bose, it may be worth waiting or watching for discounts on the current model.
- A [Dealectric page](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-aerofit-2) (an affiliate site) lists a 20% code, AFSC20, for the AeroFit 2. It also lists the price at $129.99, which conflicts with SoundGuys' $79.99 at Amazon. Compare prices before using the code.
- Prices vary by retailer and date, and the WIRED OpenRun Pro 2 review is from 2024. Check the final price at checkout.
- Open-ear designs leak sound and don't block noise. Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic.

If you tell me your budget, whether you use an iPhone or Android, and whether you wear hats or have long hair, I can narrow this to one pick.
